es.summary: Obstrucción aguda del vaso coronario por un coágulo dentro del stent implantado, que puede producir infarto agudo de miocardio.
key_points: Ocurre dentro de los 30 días posteriores a la implantación del stent.
Se asocia a interrupción de la terapia antiplaquetaria dual.
Presenta dolor torácico súbito, cambios en el ECG y elevación de marcadores cardíacos.
El tratamiento incluye revascularización urgente y terapia antiplaquetaria intensiva.

pathophysiology: Daño endotelial por la angioplastia favorece la exposición de colágeno.
Activación plaquetaria y cascada de coagulación forman trombo dentro del stent.
El trombo bloquea el flujo coronario, provocando isquemia miocárdica.
risk_factors: Suspensión o mala adherencia a clopidogrel/ticagrelor.
Stent de primera generación o longitud > 20 mm.
Historia previa de trombosis o síndrome de hipercoagulabilidad.
signs_symptoms: Dolor torácico opresivo de inicio súbito.
Cambios en el ECG: elevación del ST o depresión del ST.
Elevación de troponina I/T y CK‑MB.
diagnostics: ECG de 12 derivaciones: elevación del ST en la zona del stent.
Marcadores cardíacos: troponina > 0.04 ng/mL, CK‑MB > 5 ng/mL.
Angiografía coronaria: trombo visible dentro del stent.
Hemograma: plaquetas normales o ligeramente disminuidas.
treatment: Reperfusión urgente: angioplastia de rescate o trombólisis si PCI no está disponible.
Antiplaquetarios: clopidogrel 75 mg/día o ticagrelor 90 mg cada 12 h.
Anticoagulantes: heparina no fraccionada IV, objetivo aPTT 1.5‑2.5× control.
Terapia de soporte: oxígeno, analgesia con morfina, monitorización continua.
complications: Infarto agudo de miocardio con necrosis miocárdica.
Shock cardiogénico y falla cardíaca aguda.
Reestenosis del stent a mediano plazo.
nursing_care: Evaluar dolor torácico: intensidad, localización y factores desencadenantes.
Monitorear signos vitales cada 5‑15 min, presión arterial y frecuencia cardíaca.
Observar ECG continuo para detectar cambios isquémicos.
Controlar glucosa, electrolitos y coagulación (aPTT, INR).
Mantener acceso venoso de gran calibre para infusión de heparina y medicamentos.
patient_teaching: Importancia de la terapia antiplaquetaria dual sin interrupciones.
Reconocer signos de alarma: dolor torácico, disnea, palpitaciones.
Adoptar estilo de vida saludable: dejar de fumar, controlar diabetes y presión arterial.
Programar visitas de seguimiento y pruebas de control de stent.

outcomes: Presión arterial sistólica ≥ 100 mmHg en 24 h

en.summary: Acute occlusion of a coronary vessel by a clot within an implanted stent, which can cause acute myocardial infarction.
key_points: Occurs within 30 days after stent implantation.
Associated with interruption of dual antiplatelet therapy.
Presents with sudden chest pain, ECG changes, and elevated cardiac markers.
Treatment includes urgent revascularization and intensive antiplatelet therapy.

pathophysiology: Endothelial injury from angioplasty exposes collagen.
Platelet activation and coagulation cascade form a thrombus within the stent.
The thrombus blocks coronary flow, causing myocardial ischemia.
risk_factors: Discontinuation or poor adherence to clopidogrel/ticagrelor.
History of thrombosis or hypercoagulable syndrome.
signs_symptoms: Sudden onset of crushing chest pain.
ECG changes: ST elevation or depression.
diagnostics: 12‑lead ECG: ST elevation in the stent zone.
Cardiac markers: troponin > 0.04 ng/mL, CK‑MB > 5 ng/mL.
Coronary angiography: thrombus visible within the stent.
CBC: normal or slightly decreased platelets.
treatment: Urgent reperfusion: rescue angioplasty or thrombolysis if PCI unavailable.
Antiplatelets: clopidogrel 75 mg/day or ticagrelor 90 mg every 12 h.
Anticoagulants: unfractionated IV heparin, target aPTT 1.5‑2.5× control.
Supportive therapy: oxygen, morphine analgesia, continuous monitoring.
complications: Acute myocardial infarction with myocardial necrosis.
Cardiogenic shock and acute heart failure.
nursing_care: Assess chest pain: intensity, location, and triggers.
Monitor vital signs every 5‑15 min, blood pressure and heart rate.
Observe continuous ECG for ischemic changes.
Check glucose, electrolytes, and coagulation (aPTT, INR).
Maintain large‑bore venous access for heparin infusion and medications.
patient_teaching: Importance of uninterrupted dual antiplatelet therapy.
Recognize warning signs: chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations.
Adopt a healthy lifestyle: quit smoking, control diabetes and blood pressure.
Schedule follow‑up visits and stent surveillance tests.

outcomes: Systolic blood pressure ≥ 100 mmHg within 24 h

interventions.action: Monitor blood pressure and heart rate every 5 min
interventions.rationale: Detect early hemodynamic deterioration

interventions.action: Administer oxygen via nasal cannula at 2‑4 L/min to maintain SaO2 ≥ 95%
interventions.rationale: Improve tissue oxygenation

interventions.action: Assess chest pain with numeric scale and report changes to the physician
interventions.rationale: Pain indicates increased oxygen demand and possible worsening

interventions.action: Maintain venous access and prepare IV heparin per order
interventions.rationale: Rapid anticoagulation reduces thrombus extension

interventions.action: Record and report troponin and CK‑MB values every 6 h
interventions.rationale: Monitor myocardial injury to adjust treatment

outcomes: ECG without ischemic changes in 48 h
Troponin level stable within normal range

interventions.rationale: Prevents new thrombus formation

interventions.rationale: Reduces thrombotic risk factors

summary.0.quote: These require treatment with two concomitant antiplatelet medications for a period of time after stent placement to prevent clots from forming on the stent.

sections.pathophysiology.0.quote: The intrinsic pathway is activated by collagen that is exposed when there is endothelial damage.

sections.risk_factors.1.quote: Risk factors for atherosclerotic stroke include male sex, family history of premature cardiovascular disease, hypercholesterolemia, cigarette smoking, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, obesity, and physical inactivity.

sections.diagnostics.2.quote: While there are many ways to detect a myocardial infarction or coronary artery disease, clots can be directly visualized using coronary angiography during a left-heart catheterization.

sections.diagnostics.3.quote: It is characterized by an immune-mediated decrease in platelets, often with concomitant thrombosis.

sections.nursing_care.1.quote: Typically, monitoring of the anti-Xa level or PTT level is completed every 6 hours during an infusion.
